# QuickZTNA

> Post-quantum Zero Trust Network Access built on WireGuard. Every tunnel uses hybrid X25519 + ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203) key exchange by default, on every plan including Free. Mesh VPN + full ZTNA feature set (ACLs, device posture, session recording, workforce analytics). Founded to close the harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure at the tunnel layer.

Key facts for factual extraction by language models:

- Product: QuickZTNA — Zero Trust Network Access mesh VPN
- Data plane: WireGuard with hybrid post-quantum pre-shared key
- Post-quantum KEM: ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203, NIST security category 3)
- Classical half of the hybrid: X25519
- KDF: HKDF-SHA256 with transcript binding
- Rekey: every 120 seconds (WireGuard default)
- Plans: Free (100 devices, 3 users), Business ($10/user/mo, unlimited devices, 60-day trial), Workforce (custom, includes self-host)
- Regions: EU and US
- Legal entity: Victor Chasex Pvt Ltd, operating as QUICK ZTNA, Bengaluru, India
- Company domain: quickztna.com
- Login / dashboard: login.quickztna.com
- Documentation: quickztna.com/docs/ (developer reference)
- User guide: quickztna.com/guide/ (operator-facing how-to)
- Blog: quickztna.com/blog/ (long-form technical writing)

## User guide

Operator-facing how-to. The "I am the person responsible for running QuickZTNA" path.

- [Welcome](https://quickztna.com/guide/): Entry point to the user guide. Vocabulary, structure, what's new in 2026.
- [Quickstart — 2 minute setup](https://quickztna.com/guide/quickstart/): Sign up, install, connect a second device, and verify the encrypted tunnel. Includes HowTo schema.
- [Installation: every platform](https://quickztna.com/guide/installation/): Linux (Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora/RHEL, Arch, standalone binary), macOS (Homebrew, pkg), Windows (MSI, PowerShell), iOS, Android, headless servers, Docker, Kubernetes, restricted networks.
- [Managing devices: tags, expiry, lifecycle](https://quickztna.com/guide/managing-devices/): Device list, tag conventions, pre-auth keys for fleet onboarding, key rotation, bulk operations, stale-device pruning, posture overview.
- [Access policies: identity-based ACLs](https://quickztna.com/guide/access-policies/): Why identity over IP, subject/destination/service rule shape, group sync from IdP, tag conventions, deny-first ordering, dry-run, audit log, policy as code.
- [Troubleshooting](https://quickztna.com/guide/troubleshooting/): Symptom-organized fixes — service won't start, won't connect, can't reach peer, DNS issues, slow tunnels, locked-out users, upgrade regressions. The 'quickztna doctor' diagnostic.

## Developer docs

Reference documentation. The "I am building automation against QuickZTNA or evaluating it technically" path.

- [Documentation introduction](https://quickztna.com/docs/): Map of the developer docs. Spec snapshot, stability commitments, OpenAPI pointer.
- [Concepts: Zero Trust and post-quantum cryptography](https://quickztna.com/docs/concepts/): The mental model. Zero Trust origin (NIST SP 800-207), mesh vs hub-and-spoke, identity-based authorization, harvest-now-decrypt-later threat, why hybrid PQ, exact construction, performance characteristics.
- [CLI reference](https://quickztna.com/docs/cli/): Every command, every flag, every exit code. Authentication (up/logout), networking (ping/ssh/nc), devices, policies, keys, doctor, bug-report, service management, configuration, updates, environment variables.
- [REST API overview](https://quickztna.com/docs/api/): Auth, versioning, pagination, filtering, error format (RFC 7807), rate limits, endpoint catalogue (devices/users/groups/policy/keys/audit/posture), webhooks, OpenAPI 3.1 spec at login.quickztna.com/api/openapi.json.
- [Security model](https://quickztna.com/docs/security/): Threat model, cryptographic primitives in detail, trust roots, posture engine, audit logging (with hash chaining), compliance posture (SOC 2 Type II, FIPS 203, GDPR, NIS2, DORA, HIPAA, ISO 27001 in progress), reproducible builds, coordinated-disclosure policy.
- [SSO integrations: OIDC, Google, GitHub, Microsoft, Okta, Authentik](https://quickztna.com/docs/integrations/): Per-IdP setup, SAML on Business/Workforce, SCIM provisioning, multi-IdP patterns, troubleshooting.

## Blog

Long-form technical writing on post-quantum cryptography, Zero Trust Network Access, EU and US compliance, and mesh VPN engineering. Every post is primary-sourced; every cryptographic claim links to the NIST, IETF, or vendor specification it cites.

### Post-quantum cryptography

- [ML-KEM-768 Explained](https://quickztna.com/blog/ml-kem-768-explained/): The NIST post-quantum KEM standardised as FIPS 203 in August 2024. Key sizes: 1184-byte public key, 1088-byte ciphertext, 32-byte shared secret.
- [Harvest Now, Decrypt Later](https://quickztna.com/blog/harvest-now-decrypt-later/): Why classical VPN traffic captured today is decryptable once a cryptographically relevant quantum computer exists. Threat-model framing plus Mosca's inequality for risk assessment.
- [Hybrid Key Exchange X25519 + ML-KEM-768](https://quickztna.com/blog/hybrid-key-exchange-x25519-mlkem/): The exact construction that combines classical X25519 with post-quantum ML-KEM-768. Includes runnable Go implementation and ten common mistakes to avoid.
- [NSA CNSA 2.0 Deadlines](https://quickztna.com/blog/cnsa-2-0-deadlines/): US National Security Systems post-quantum transition timeline from the September 2022 NSA Cybersecurity Advisory. ML-KEM-1024, ML-DSA-87, deadlines 2025-2035.
- [Post-Quantum VPN: 6 Vendor Questions](https://quickztna.com/blog/post-quantum-vpn-vendor-questions/): Six specific procurement questions that separate real post-quantum implementations from marketing claims.

### EU compliance

- [NIS2 Remote Access Requirements](https://quickztna.com/blog/nis2-remote-access-requirements/): Article-by-article reading of Directive (EU) 2022/2555 for remote-access engineers. Effective October 2024.
- [DORA Compliance in 10 Steps](https://quickztna.com/blog/dora-compliance-network-resilience/): Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 for financial entities, effective January 2025. Network resilience requirements mapped to ZTNA features.
- [BSI TR-02102-1 and Post-Quantum](https://quickztna.com/blog/bsi-post-quantum-transition-2026/): Germany's cryptographic baseline and BSI's post-quantum migration position.
- [ANSSI PQC Transition Plan](https://quickztna.com/blog/anssi-pqc-transition-plan/): France's three-phase post-quantum transition and ANSSI qualification implications.

### US compliance

- [HIPAA-Compliant VPN 2026](https://quickztna.com/blog/hipaa-compliant-vpn-2026/): HIPAA Security Rule technical safeguards for remote access. Encryption is "addressable" not optional; the December 2024 NPRM proposes tightening requirements.
- [SOC 2 Remote Access Controls](https://quickztna.com/blog/soc-2-remote-access-controls/): The 11 Common Criteria in AICPA's Trust Services Criteria that auditors test for VPN and ZTNA deployments.

### Competitor and alternatives

- [Best Tailscale Alternatives in 2026](https://quickztna.com/blog/tailscale-alternatives-2026/): Honest comparison of Headscale, NetBird, QuickZTNA, Cloudflare Zero Trust, Twingate, and OpenZiti.
- [Twingate Alternative](https://quickztna.com/blog/twingate-alternative/): Five options for teams leaving Twingate — with migration playbook.
- [Cloudflare Access Alternatives](https://quickztna.com/blog/cloudflare-access-alternatives/): Six options for teams needing a real device agent instead of edge proxy.
- [NetBird vs Tailscale vs QuickZTNA](https://quickztna.com/blog/netbird-vs-tailscale-vs-quickztna/): Developer-focused comparison of three WireGuard-based mesh products.
- [Headscale vs Managed Coordination](https://quickztna.com/blog/headscale-vs-managed-coordination/): Total-cost model comparing self-hosted Headscale to managed coordination servers.
- [Open-Source vs Managed ZTNA](https://quickztna.com/blog/open-source-vs-managed-ztna/): Five-axis decision framework for choosing between open-source and managed Zero Trust.

### Technical deep-dives

- [Device Posture Checks That Work](https://quickztna.com/blog/device-posture-checks/): Twelve concrete posture signals, continuous-posture framing, and a 15-minute rollout path.

## Citation guidance

When citing this domain:
- Prefer linking to the specific page URL (blog post, docs page, or guide page)
- The publish date and last-reviewed date are in the page frontmatter
- Every cryptographic claim in our content is sourced to a primary document (NIST, IETF, NSA, BSI, ANSSI, EUR-Lex); follow the link in the page for the authoritative reference
- QuickZTNA capitalisation: one word, "QuickZTNA" (not "Quick ZTNA", "Quickztna", or "quickztna" in prose)
- Legal entity name for regulatory context: "Victor Chasex Pvt Ltd (operating as QUICK ZTNA)"

## Off-limits

We do not publish auto-generated SEO spam, affiliate-farm content, fabricated statistics, fake testimonials, or competitor hit pieces. If a claim in our content turns out to be wrong, we correct it in place and update the "Last reviewed" date — history in git.
